title: Selector grammar edges
blurb: Parse matrix for ::highlight(*) spellings, which highlight pseudo-elements * matches, and a highlight literally named "*".
question: Which spellings of ::highlight(*) parse, does * reach ::selection or spelling errors, and can a highlight named "*" be targeted separately?
result: Accepted: ::highlight(*), ::highlight( * ), p::highlight(*), :root ::highlight(*), *::highlight(*), ::highlight(\*); rejected: *a, a-comma-*, * *, empty, :hover and ::after suffixes. * matches custom highlights only. ::highlight(\*) targets a highlight named "*" and beats the universal rule in paint, but getComputedStyle(el, '::highlight(*)') always answers for the universal rule.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 158.0.8127.36 (Linux, headless, no flags) on 2026-11-27

friction.summary: getComputedStyle(el, '::highlight(never-registered)') reports the universal rule's values; computed style does not consult the highlight registry.
friction.repro: Add ::highlight(*) { text-decoration: underline wavy } and read getComputedStyle(p, '::highlight(nope)').textDecorationStyle: 'wavy'.
friction.workaround: Check CSS.highlights.has(name) before trusting a computed highlight style.
